II
Do we belong to the number of those who suffer in this
world? Those whose vision penetrates beyond the sphere of
the visible to that of the eternal and invisible? Are we among
those who hope and wait in expectancy for the One who is
to come? This is the critical Advent question. If we do belong
to this number then we must in our turn, like the Baptist,
address to Jesus the question: "Are you the One who is to
come?" Is Jesus Christ in truth the One in whom all our
hopes and longings find their fulfilment? Is He the one who
brings in the kingdom of peace?
Were He the One-then surely He must already have
established His kingdom! If He is the destined Messiah, He
has come already indeed, long ago. More than 1900 years
ago! And has the world changed as a result of His coming?
The Christian Church affirms just this: He has come and has
ushered in the new age, and yet He is still the One who is to
come. In what sense may this be understood?
What answer does Jesus give to the Baptist? Go and tell
John what you hear and see! "The blind receive their sight
and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear,
the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news
preached to them. And blessed is he who takes no offence
at me."

neither yes nor no. He refers the questioner to the things
